title: Cisco Password Types: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Picture a ring of castle keys. Some keys are strong. Others anyone can copy in seconds.

lines.t: Some can be copied in seconds

scenes.heading: The castle key ring
scenes.narration: Cisco stores passwords in different types. Type zero is plain text, written on the key itself. Type seven is scrambled, but anyone can unscramble it. Type five is an M D five hash, which is much better. Types eight and nine are the strongest, and nine uses scrypt.

scenes.heading: Use these
scenes.narration: Pick the strong options. Use enable secret with the scrypt type. Service password encryption only makes type seven. And check what's stored.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Type seven is reversible. Enable password is plain text. It only converts plain text to type seven.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Use enable secret, never enable password. Type seven is weak. Type nine is the strongest. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva passwords lab.
